niche: a state sentencing commission projecting how many of the people released to parole in 2027 will be back in prison within two years, the first cohort released under an act that ends returns to prison except on a new court commitment, when the parole board answered most parolees' arrests in the record by revocation before any court could
answer: Carry a two-year return rate of 20 per cent for the 6,466 people the Department expects to release to parole in 2027.
answer_source: submission.md, 1. Final Recommendation (generator/deliver.py from the pack; generator/verify.py recomputes)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who links the four agencies' records, reads the Act correctly and keeps only the record's new-commitment returns, modelling them on the obvious covariates, files 5 per cent (10 per cent with revocations as competing exits, about 12 per cent counting the arrests that ended in a Department sentence per day at liberty, which both stage 4 readers filed as 10), when the parolees' arrests the Board answered by revocation will be prosecuted and turned into prison commitments at the courts' own rate by charge grade, which files 20 per cent.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a release cohort's two-year return-to-prison rate estimated the way a corrections forecaster does it, from the arrest process and the courts' conversion of arrests into prison sentences by offence class, with the route each past return took read from the board's and the courts' records; with hospital readmissions or utility disconnections in place of returns there is no second institution whose processing the act hands the same behaviour to.

driver: The decisive quantity is the forward rate of an outcome that the record reaches through two processing routes, one of which a filed change closes: the rate the record shows through the remaining route understates it because the closed route pre-empted that route for most events, so only sending each event the closed route took through the remaining route's own conversion, by event class, sizes it.
driver_concrete: Under Act 26-114 a parolee returns to prison only on a new court commitment, and the record's new-commitment returns are few because the Board revoked about a third of parolees' arrests (four in five in Garrison, one in five in Corliss) before any court decided them; those arrests will now go to court and become prison commitments at the courts' own rate by charge grade, so the two-year rate is the arrest process per day out of custody times that conversion and its timing, 20 per cent against the record's 5.
stump: A competent solver keeps only the returns the Act still allows, models each 2027 release's chance of a new-commitment admission within two years on the record's complete releases and files 5 per cent; the step that lands it there is reading the record's new-commitment returns as what parolees' arrests produce, when the Board answered about a third of parolees' arrests by revoking them before any court could, and under the Act those arrests go to court and become prison commitments at the courts' own rate for their charge grade, which files 20 per cent.

lineage.driver: Where a limit is exceeded only in one cell of a recurring cycle that one component of demand dominates, the record's growth measured over the whole cycle is a mix of components growing at different rates, and an outside condition that differed across the record's periods moved some components more than others, so carrying the whole-cycle growth to that cell or reading the condition's effect as trend misranks the candidates; only the cell's own growth with the condition held fixed ranks them right.
lineage.driver_concrete: Tolland Bridge on Tolland Road, 2.6 m wide and rated for 650 cyclists an hour, overflows only between 08:00 and 09:00 on weekday mornings, a commuting hour that grows 11 to 14 per cent a year once each day's weather is held fixed, while the bridge's daily total, half of it midday riding that is flat or falling, grew 8.6 per cent from 2025 to 2026, and the Estuary Path's leisure riding rose with the hot, dry summer of 2026 well beyond its trend; replaying the three summers at each counter's growth in total riders puts Estuary Path first and Tolland Road fifth, and each counter's growth by hour and day group with each day's rain and temperature held fixed puts Tolland Road first.
lineage.stump: A competent solver replays the three recorded summers at each counter's 2025 to 2026 growth in total riders and files Estuary Path, because the hot, dry summer of 2026 lifted the path's leisure riding and that rise is read as trend, while Tolland Bridge's daily total hides how fast the weekday 08:00 commuting hour that crowds it is growing; only each counter's growth at its own hour and day group, with each day's rain and temperature held fixed, files Tolland Road.
lineage.analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms both exports, reads every capacity and rule correctly and replays the three summers at each counter's 2025 to 2026 growth in total riders files Estuary Path; growth by hour without weather and weather-held daily growth file Estuary Path too, and only hour-level growth with rain and temperature held files Tolland Road.
lineage.domain_test: The quantity that decides the call is the forecast number of days next summer on which a counted segment's two-way hourly cycle flow exceeds its design capacity, estimated the way a transport planner forecasts cycle demand, by trip-purpose growth at the hour that binds with weather held fixed; with beds or megawatt-hours in place of cyclists there is no commuting peak growing against declining leisure riding and no weather elasticity of leisure trips.
